title: The down window gates every request of the lookup revalidation, not only a source's first page request
goal: The search host (api.github.com, export.arxiv.org, the Learn search), candidate pages, the made-up sibling and a pinned url's repository request read and record the host's down window as a source's own page does, so two searches against a host that does not accept a connection make one request, not two; when a source's url answers a redirect to another host that does not accept a connection, the down window is recorded for the target's host, not the source's own host that answered. Found by the SP-u5q37ds3 review (_tools/factdiff.py search_urls, page_doc, madeup_text and detect_pass, provider.repository_state and the provider.request hops).

gates.question: How does a request of the lookup revalidation read and record a host's down window, given that provider.request is also the detection runs' request and tests stub it?
options: gated_request under down_window: provider.gated_request, called by each lookup request site, gated by a process flag that factdiff.revalidate sets with provider.down_window
lookup parameter: a lookup flag threaded through detect_source, resolve, elsewhere, page_doc, search_urls, madeup_text and repository_state
inside request: the gate and the recording inside provider.request itself
gates.recommendation: gated_request under down_window: provider.gated_request, called by each lookup request site, gated by a process flag that factdiff.revalidate sets with provider.down_window

gates.question: What becomes of detect_pass's own host_down check before a source and its host_seen call after it, which take the source's own url, once every request records the window of the host it went to?
options: removed: the source's page request is gated and records its hosts itself, the redirect target included, so the per-source check and call would only repeat it, for the source's host
kept: both stay beside the gated requests
gates.recommendation: removed: the source's page request is gated and records its hosts itself, the redirect target included, so the per-source check and call would only repeat it, for the source's host

gates.question: A redirect hop of a request leads into a host that is in its window: is the hop refused, or only the outcome recorded?
options: record only: the hop is followed, as the goal names only the recording of the target's window, and the window it finds ends or doubles as any request's
refuse the hop: provider._Chain raises a URLError for a target in its window
gates.recommendation: record only: the hop is followed, as the goal names only the recording of the target's window, and the window it finds ends or doubles as any request's
gates.answer: record only: the hop is followed, as the goal names only the recording of the target's window, and the window it finds ends or doubles as any request's

notes: Merged from ST-ecxt66tw at the 2026-10-13 draft triage: its goal is the goal's second clause, its check revalidate_down_window_redirect_target the second check. Premise: detect_pass calls host_seen(url, error) with the source's own url (factdiff.py:1341), and provider.request keeps final=url when a redirect hop fails to connect, so the source's host gets the window. Rare: only 11 of 2621 sources redirect cross-host, none to a known-dead host. Premise: factdiff.madeup_text and page_doc call provider.request with no provider.host_down check; with api.github.com in its window, one madeup_text and one page_doc made 2 requests (run 2026-10-13 at base, planted window). Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 4 of 15, "Freshness and census: the down window, the confirmable rule, soft 404s, unlocated anchors and mirror licences"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed. Its checks' tests drive revalidate (the lookup path) with provider.request stubbed, not detect_pass alone. Test ids are near the ceiling: extend the existing revalidate test and append both selector words to its name, a new id only when none does.
